messages:
andrea: quick sync—thinking about where we should do PII redaction for traces/logs. options: SDK/client, edge-ingest, or central server-side. what are the interface boundaries and tradeoffs?

devon: short answer: there is no one-size. client redact = better privacy surface and less data ever leaves customer, but you lose fidelity for server-side enrichments and debug. edge-ingest redact gives config centralization and keeps clients thin. server-side redact is easiest to iterate on but costs storage and risk.

liam: also legal/retention concerns. if we redact at client we cannot satisfy e-Discovery requests without a crypto-hidden backup. propose optional encrypted raw store for legal holds if client-redact is chosen.

maya: plus metric/cardinality impact. removing vs hashing fields changes downstream keys. hashing must be salted per-tenant and deterministic to keep billing/attribution stable. unsalted hashes are risky.

andrea: rough interface idea: SDK can send metadata header: x-redact-policy: "client"|"edge"|"server" and x-redact-list (JSON pointer array). server honors tenant policy and overrides if needed. fallback: server enforces more strict policy for regulated tenants.

devon: prototype scrub config we discussed:
```json
{
  "version":"1",
  "rules":[
    {"path":"$.user.email","action":"hash","salted":true},
    {"path":"$.user.phone","action":"remove"},
    {"path":"$.request.headers.authorization","action":"remove"}
  ]
}
```
Use JSON Pointers so SDKs and ingest can implement cheaply.

liam: important callout for cost attribution: hashed user identifiers must be stable across requests and across model/route shards. we need deterministic-salt per-tenant using KMS; and a rotation plan that preserves historic billing groups (rotate by re-deriving old->new mapping in billing window).

maya: perf tradeoff: write-time scrub = more CPU at ingest path, increases p95 latency. read-time scrub = cheaper ingest but keeps raw data around and higher storage costs + privacy surface. suggest a hybrid: default write-time removal for heavy regex rules, allow read-time enrich for low-volume debug flows. also add `scrub-budget-ms` hint in header to select fast-path (no complex regex).

obs-bot: deploybot: OBS_SCRUB_MODE=server rolled to staging; integration tests: 2/3 green, one flaky with payloads >1MB causing timeouts. captured logs: "ingest-scrub: exceeded_regex_budget".

andrea: next steps RFC-followup items: 1) formalize header contract & JSON-pointer schema 2) define deterministic-salt KMS flow + rotation semantics 3) scrub budgeting & hinting (scrub-budget-ms) 4) encrypted raw-store option for legal holds 5) metrics to measure billing-key fragmentation.

andrea: who can own the RFC doc? devon/ liam? also need an API/SDK owner to align implementations. :thumbsup:

devon: I can take the RFC draft this week, will include perf numbers and rough sequence diagrams.

liam: I'll drive KMS design and the deterministic-hash spec. will add a small proto for salt lookup service.

maya: I'll prototype `scrub-budget-ms` routing in the gateway and run latency tests.

andrea: awesome. i'll schedule a 30m follow-up and link the draft. thanks all :raised_hands:
